questions.stem: In Example 5, what is the probability of event A given that event B has occurred?
questions.solution: In Example 5, event A is getting a 4 on the third throw, and event B is getting a 6 on the first and 5 on the second throw. The probability of A given B is calculated as P(A ∩ B)/P(B). Since there is only one favorable outcome (6,5,4) out of 216 total outcomes, P(A ∩ B) = 1/216. P(B) = 1/36, so P(A|B) = (1/216)/(1/36) = 1/6. The correct answer is 1/6. The other options are incorrect because they do not match the calculated probabilities.

questions.stem: A patient has a 40% chance of having a heart attack. A meditation and yoga course reduces the risk by 30%, and a drug reduces it by 25%. The patient chooses either option with equal probability. If the patient suffers a heart attack, what is the probability that they chose the meditation and yoga course?
questions.solution: The patient has a 40% chance of having a heart attack. Choosing meditation reduces the risk to 40% * (1 - 30%) = 28%, and choosing the drug reduces it to 40% * (1 - 25%) = 30%. questions.stem: A die is thrown three times. Events A and B are defined as follows: A : 4 on the third throw, B : 6 on the first and 5 on the second throw. What is the probability of A given that B has already occurred?
questions.solution: The sample space for three dice rolls has 216 outcomes. Event B (6 on the first and 5 on the second) has 6 outcomes (since the third die can be 1-6). Event A ∩ B (4 on the third throw) has 1 outcome (6,5,4). So P(A|B) = P(A ∩ B)/P(B) = (1/216)/(6/216) = 1/6.
